subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO checklist / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, FintechCo SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Hi Alex / Fintech SRE team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the open discussion. Per our demo and the perf walkthrough, I wanted to capture the performance targets you gave and outline immediate next steps so we can size a PoC load test and proposal.

SLO / perf targets you mentioned (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- Peak sustained throughput: ~500 QPS across 3 regions (primarily us-west)
- Concurrency requirement: up to 200 concurrent user sessions (with burst to 400 for short windows)
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 700ms for single-turn (non-streamed)  — streaming first-byte <= 120ms, tailing tokens steady-state < 50ms/token
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for chat UI with server-sent-events or websocket; must support partial responses + function/tool-calling semantics
- Payload: average prompt size ~1.5k tokens; 95th percentile ~3k tokens
- Availability/SLAs: targeting 99.9% for inference endpoint (we can discuss Dedicated options for stricter SLAs)

Attachments: I attached a quick SLO checklist (FintechCo_SLO_Checklist_v1.xlsx) and the high-level logs from our demo run (load-test-logs-20270214.zip).

Proposed next steps / MAP (mutual action plan):
1) Confirm final SLO numbers by EOD Mon 2/15 (you + SRE) — so we can size capacity.
2) Redwood to run a 2-hour PoC load test (we'll simulate your token distribution) — target week of 2/22.
3) Deliver PoC report with latency percentiles, cost estimate (per-token / hour), and autoscaling recommendations.
4) If PoC meets targets, scope Dedicated reservation with canary rollout plan.

Can you confirm the items above and share any additional constraints (e.g., IP allowlists, data residency, or security questionnaires) we should include in the PoC?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, FintechCo SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 18:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Marissa — thanks, that is a solid capture. A few clarifications from our side:
- Throughput: 500 QPS is correct as a near-term target, but we'd like the PoC to show linear scaling to 1k QPS (we have seasonal peaks).
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent *active* sessions (users sending tokens). We also have ~1.5k idle sessions that we keep KV state for; confirm Redwood can handle session KV caching separately from active concurrency.
- Latency: your numbers are in the right ballpark. For streaming, we care most about first-byte < 120ms and that there is less than 200ms jitter for first 10 tokens under load.
- Security: we will require a completed security questionnaire and proof of SOC 2 (or timeline). We'll start the procurement paperwork after PoC.

Couple questions for the PoC: what model variants will you run (float32 vs quantized), and can you provide an initial cost estimate per 1M tokens for the PoC run? Also, please confirm whether the PoC environment supports cloud-region pinning (we prefer us-west-primary with failover to us-east).

Thanks — Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, FintechCo SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the clarifications. I've updated the checklist and sketched initial answers below; attached is SLO checklist v1 (spreadsheet) with the updated numbers.

Quick answers inline:
- Scaling target: we'll run the PoC to validate linear scaling to 1k QPS; we'll also validate autoscaling behavior for bursts to 1.5k QPS for short windows.
- Session KV caching: Redwood's runtime supports KV prefix caching and separate in-memory session cache; we'll size memory for your 1.5k idle sessions in the PoC config.
- Models: PoC will run the recommended open model (redwood-llm-v2) in int8 quantized profile + a float32 baseline for comparison. We'll include perf delta and cost delta in the report.
- Cost estimate: initial ballpark for PoC run is ~ $1,200 per 1M tokens (quantized) — final number depends on concurrency and caching. We'll provide a more precise estimate with the load-test config.
- Region pinning: yes — PoC supports region pinning (us-west primary, us-east failover).

Next steps (updated):
- You confirm final SLO numbers by EOD 2/15 (Alex + SRE).
- Aditya / Rishi to schedule the PoC load test with Fintech SRE and provide the test config (token distribution + QPS curve).
- Redwood to run PoC 2/22–2/23 (2-hour run + 1-hour cooldown) and deliver report by 2/25.

Aditya / Rishi — can you take point on the PoC schedule + test config? I put the attachments in this thread.

Best,
Marissa
